title: The Sugarcane Raid Becomes a Courtly Spectacle

blocks.text: The Singhs greet the order with delight and theatrical energy. At a beat on the war drum they arm themselves, rush out under observation from Delhi, and prepare to show a spectacle of looting and plundering that is half demonstration and half rough comedy.

The performance is exuberant and physical. Riders and footmen plunged deep into the river Yamuna, burst into the sugarcane, and return laughing, pulling at beards and turbans of each other while carts, horses, and elephants become loaded with the pillaged sugarcane sticks.

What the emperor witnesses is not merely disorder but a controlled display of Sikh ferocity, mobility, and irreverent confidence. The page ends with Delhi entertained, instructed, and reminded that Khalsa energy cannot be reduced to court etiquette.
